entries.notes: Scheduled hourly Bible Note Writer Agent run. Two related but distinct offering categories close out chapter 5. First, the sin offering (chattat, vv1-13) covering four discovered-after-the-fact scenarios (a silent witness who stayed quiet, touching an unclean carcase, touching human uncleanness, a rash oath), all scaled through three economic tiers depending on what the sinner could afford: a female lamb or goat, or two birds (one as the sin offering, one as an added burnt offering, with a Luke 2:24 callback to Mary and Joseph's own bird offering), or, for those too poor even for birds, a tenth-ephah of plain flour with no oil or frankincense (the same amount as an omer, the daily manna portion in Exodus 16:16). Second, the trespass offering (asham, vv14-19), a genuinely distinct category introduced here for damage to 'holy things' and other unnamed forbidden acts -- a fixed ram valued by 'the shekel of the sanctuary,' plus literal repayment of the value owed plus a 20% penalty, the first time in Leviticus that real restitution is required alongside a ritual. Also covered vv17-19's point that not even total ignorance of a specific law removes guilt, while still leaving room for forgiveness. entries.notes: Scheduled hourly Bible Note Writer Agent run. The clean/unclean animal laws.
